doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Florida life and the jazz scene
title: The South Florida music scene and Heat Beat magazine
summary: A new listings magazine helps unify the spread-out South Florida scene.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Is there a live music scene where you live in Florida of any extent?

Yeah, it’s getting better too. I think the main reason is about a year ago, maybe a little over a year ago, a guy by the name of Bruce Scott started a magazine, like one of those small booklet-sized magazines, styled after the Hot House, in New York. It’s a listing. It’s a place where all the listings can appear, and the clubs, and record companies, and whoever else in the music business, whether it be artists or big companies, whatever, can advertise whatever it is. Advertise a concert, advertise a record, advertise promotion for something. And it’s got a couple of articles and a whole bunch of listings and a bunch of ads. And because of that, now it’s possible to see, I mean the South Florida scene is spread out in three counties, Dade, Broward and Palm Beach. So between just north of Palm Beach and south of Miami that’s a big area. So it’s hard to — you might be aware of one little scene in one town, and another in a little town will all look very disjointed © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-

and fractured, but now, to somebody coming to that area, a tourist coming to that area can get this one book and see, this is happening in South Beach and this is happening in Ft. Lauderdale, and this is happening in Palm Beach County. And it’s sort of something like to keep track of the music scene as a whole, taking the music scene as a whole. Because in my opinion the problem with music is just like the same problem that we have politically and everything now with everything splitting off into — like cable TV — instead of having three channels, three ideologies, now we have twenty seven thousand and we have forty seven different music categories. And that’s what I like — the thing is called Heat Beat, the thing that’s styled after the Hot House, it’s call the Heat Beat. And it contains all the listings for south Florida. And it’s just nice to see it all in one place. It gives you an idea that there is a scene there. And now with all the different clubs and stuff sort of competing for attention in the Heat Beat, it gives it a forum. It gives the whole scene, as one whole scene, a forum to like check each other out — and you can just imagine — well their ad was — and we’re going to do bigger than them next month, and that kind of thing. So I think it’s healthy for the scene.
